articles.title: EVAOLD trial provides guidance on treating older patients after a heart attack
articles.summary_3_sentences: The EVAOLD trial found that a routine invasive approach should not be replaced by a more selective approach in older patients with the most common type of heart attack. The findings were presented in a Hot Line session at ESC Congress 2026.

articles.title: New data presented on the use of coronary artery calcium for cardiovascular risk assessment
articles.summary_3_sentences: ESC Congress 2026 data showed no difference in major cardiovascular events when statin initiation was guided by coronary artery calcium compared with traditional risk-factor assessment. The report addresses how best to assess cardiovascular risk and decide on preventive statin therapy.

articles.title: Two imaging techniques equally as effective to guide complex stenting
articles.summary_3_sentences: Optical coherence tomography was noninferior to intravascular ultrasound for guiding stenting in patients with left main coronary artery disease. The results were presented at ESC Congress 2026 and compare two imaging strategies for complex coronary intervention.

articles.title: Immediate coronary angiography fails to boost survival after cardiac arrest, trial finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: The DISCO trial and a meta-analysis found that immediate coronary angiography did not improve 30-day survival compared with a deferred strategy after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in patients without ST-segment elevation. The findings were presented in a Hot Line session at ESC Congress 2026.

articles.title: Activation of community first responders did not improve short-term survival after cardiac arrest
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study presented at ESC Congress 2026 reported that activating community first responders did not improve 30-day survival for patients with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. The finding evaluates a community-based emergency response strategy for cardiac arrest care.

articles.title: New insights on the optimal duration of antiplatelet therapy after stent implantation
articles.summary_3_sentences: The A-CLOSE trial found that antiplatelet monotherapy reduced bleeding, while dual therapy offered greater protection against cardiovascular events in high-ischemic-risk patients 12 months after stent implantation. The results were presented at ESC Congress 2026 and published in the New England Journal of Medicine.

articles.title: Laughter therapy can help people with COPD breathe more easily
articles.summary_3_sentences: A clinical trial in people with COPD found that laughter therapy reduced breathing difficulties and performed as well as traditional breathing exercises. The research was presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress in Barcelona.

articles.title: In a third of cases, AI chatbots wrongly reassure sleep apnea patients that their symptoms aren't serious
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress found that AI chatbots wrongly reassured sleep apnea patients in about one-third of cases that their symptoms were not serious. The report says this could discourage some patients from seeking specialist referral.

articles.title: Bacteria in classroom dust associated with reduced lung function in children
articles.summary_3_sentences: Common bacteria found in classroom dust were associated with reduced lung function in children, according to research presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress. The findings may inform efforts to make schools healthier environments for developing lungs.

articles.title: Origins of COPD may lie in how some children's lungs develop, but only when they are exposed to polluted air
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that COPD risk may be shaped decades before diagnosis by how children's lungs grow and develop. The reported link appears to depend on exposure to polluted air, highlighting a possible interaction between early lung development and environment.

articles.title: Nightly Pill Reduces Sleep Apnea Breathing Interruptions
articles.summary_3_sentences: A nightly pill reduced breathing interruptions by about 44% in patients with sleep apnea in a phase 3 trial. The report focuses on reductions in repeated breathing interruptions when the pill was taken nightly.

articles.title: Sleep Disruptions Linked to Genetic Alzheimer's Disease Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Micro-awakenings at night were linked with genetic risk for Alzheimer's disease. The finding suggests that brief sleep disruptions may be a measurable sleep-pattern marker associated with later Alzheimer's risk, though the summary does not establish causation.

articles.title: Hypothyroidism Linked to Higher Risk of Sleep Apnea
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study reported that people with hypothyroidism are more likely to experience obstructive sleep apnea. The finding identifies an association between reduced thyroid function and OSA.

articles.title: Focal therapy use remains uncommon in nonmetastatic prostate cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A JAMA research letter reported that focal therapy remains uncommon among patients with nonmetastatic prostate cancer across risk groups. About half of focal therapy use among recipients was categorized as inappropriate.

articles.title: Targeting cell division protein CDK2 could boost immunotherapy response across a wide range of cancers
articles.summary_3_sentences: Dana-Farber researchers reported that CDK2 inhibitors, now being tested in narrower cancer settings, may have broader potential when combined with immunotherapy. The article describes this as a possible way to improve immunotherapy response across multiple cancers.

articles.title: People affected by cancer need a stronger voice in shaping generative AI for oncology, review finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A scoping review found that only 32 studies among 2,441 records examined how cancer patients, survivors and caregivers view generative AI in cancer care. The authors argue that people affected by cancer need more involvement in shaping oncology AI tools.

articles.title: Partnering Prostate Cancer and Cardiovascular Care for Improved Outcomes
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article highlights cardiovascular risk factors among prostate cancer patients and argues for coordination between cancer and cardiovascular care. It notes that untreated cardiovascular conditions can create additional concerns for these patients.

articles.title: Oncology Research Company BioNTech Announces New CEO
articles.summary_3_sentences: BioNTech announced Guido Oelkers as its next chief executive officer. Oelkers is scheduled to take over on February 1, 2027, marking a planned leadership change at the oncology research company.

articles.title: Experimental drug targets "undruggable" cancer protein
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental drug reportedly disrupted the activity of MYC, a cancer protein often described as difficult to target. The article presents the work as an advance in drug-directed strategies against MYC.

topic_groups.topic: Brain, Cognition, Mental Health and Neurodevelopment

articles.title: Self-control matures later than working memory in adolescence, large analysis finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large analysis found that self-control matures later than working memory during adolescence. The report places the finding within the broader mental, emotional and social development that occurs between childhood and adulthood.

articles.title: Ultra-fast microscope design captures zebrafish brain seizures
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists used an ultra-fast microscope design to capture seizure activity spreading through a living zebrafish brain in three dimensions. The work provides a preclinical view of how seizures propagate across zebrafish brain tissue.

articles.title: A single workout may help protect memory after a short night's sleep
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses research on whether a single workout can help protect memory after one short night of sleep. It frames the question against evidence that sleep loss can impair learning, storage and recall.

articles.title: Cerebroid study hints at how maternal inflammation may influence fetal brain development
articles.summary_3_sentences: A cerebroid study explored how heightened maternal immune responses during pregnancy might affect fetal brain development. The article emphasizes that the work addresses mechanisms behind an association that has been observed in prior studies.

articles.title: NFL settlement testing may miss measurable cognitive decline in players with advanced CTE
articles.summary_3_sentences: Boston University researchers studied cognitive symptoms in NFL players with confirmed CTE who had undergone neuropsychological testing while alive. The report says settlement testing may miss measurable cognitive decline in players with advanced CTE.

articles.title: Traumatic brain injury recovery follows different neurological paths with age
articles.summary_3_sentences: Texas A&M research suggests that traumatic brain injury recovery may follow different neurological paths depending on age. The article notes that flexibility in younger brains may help compensate for injury while also masking harmful changes that continue beneath the surface.

articles.title: Children's suicide-related emergency visits spiked by 74% in the US between 2016-2022
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study by Northwestern University and Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago found that suicide-related emergency visits by children rose 74% in the United States between 2016 and 2022. The findings point to a substantial increase in pediatric mental-health crises presenting to emergency care.

articles.title: IBD Linked to Higher Risk of Psychiatric Disorders
articles.summary_3_sentences: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease were reported to have an increased risk of psychiatric disorders. The elevated risk was described as beginning two to three years after IBD diagnosis.

articles.title: HEPA Air Purifiers May Boost Cognition After Age 40
articles.summary_3_sentences: Use of a HEPA purifier for one month was linked to 12% faster performance on cognitive tests in adults aged 40 and older. The report describes an association with cognitive-test speed rather than a clinical diagnosis.

articles.title: Early Social Media Use Linked to Anxiety, Depression
articles.summary_3_sentences: Starting social media use at a younger age was associated with more symptoms of anxiety and depression. The report identifies an association between early exposure and mental-health symptoms.

articles.title: Human brain organoids gain sense of time and space
articles.summary_3_sentences: Two recent studies advanced research on human brain organoids, including work suggesting that organoids can record the passage of time. The studies also examined how organoid models represent or gain a sense of space.

articles.title: Shingles Vaccine Linked to 24% Lower Dementia Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults who received the Shingrix shingles vaccine were reported to have a 24% lower risk of dementia diagnosis within four years. The finding is an association between vaccination and later dementia diagnoses.

articles.title: Ozempic Shows Promise in Bipolar Disorder
articles.summary_3_sentences: Semaglutide, sold as Ozempic and Wegovy, was linked to a lower risk of psychiatric hospitalization among people with bipolar disorder. The report suggests possible relevance for psychiatric outcomes but describes an association rather than established causality.

articles.title: High-Dose Vitamin D Linked to Better Cognition
articles.summary_3_sentences: Daily intake of at least 5,000 IU of vitamin D was linked to better cognitive scores among older adults. The report concerns cognitive scores, not a stated dementia diagnosis or treatment effect.

articles.title: Mini-brains show how maternal inflammation alters development
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes mini-brain research examining how maternal inflammation alters development. The visible information identifies maternal inflammation and developmental change as the focus, without additional experimental details.

articles.title: Modifiable Risks Linked to Dementia-Related Brain Damage
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that almost half of dementia cases may be linked to modifiable risk factors. Smoking and high blood pressure are identified as examples of changeable risks connected with dementia-related brain damage.

articles.title: Evidence points to yogurt as a nutrient-dense part of healthy diets
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews evidence describing yogurt as a nutrient-dense part of healthy diets. It notes that health claims about yogurt have circulated for hundreds of years.

articles.title: Link between IBS-C and Gut Microbiome Metabolites
articles.summary_3_sentences: A 2020 study identified two gut microbiome metabolites that were altered in people with irritable bowel syndrome with constipation. The article describes measurable differences in gut microbial metabolism among affected individuals.

articles.title: Antifungal Drug May Ease IBD Disease Activity
articles.summary_3_sentences: A commonly used antifungal medication may improve disease activity in some patients with inflammatory bowel disease. The report focuses on IBD disease activity rather than the drug's usual use for yeast infections.

articles.title: Coffee May Improve Many Aspects of Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that coffee may offer benefits for heart health, metabolism and body composition. The summary presents these as potential health influences of coffee consumption.

articles.title: How Plant-Based Foods Boost the Gut Microbiome & Human Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes how plant-based foods may benefit health partly through effects on the gut microbiome. It focuses on links between dietary plant foods, microorganisms and human health.

articles.title: How Metaproteomics Can Advance Gut Microbiome Research
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains how metaproteomics can advance research on the human gut microbiome. It highlights the value of studying microbial proteins in a gut community that has been linked to many health conditions.

articles.title: Older athletes show aging need not bring major losses in fitness or independence
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports on a high-profile cohort of older professional athletes whose experience suggests aging does not necessarily bring major losses in fitness or independence. The provided summary is limited but frames the item around athletic aging and functional capacity.

articles.title: Six-month community program improves attention and diet scores in older adults
articles.summary_3_sentences: A six-month community program improved attention and diet scores in older adults. The article frames the program as a scalable alternative to more resource-intensive multidomain lifestyle interventions for brain health.

articles.title: Actin Scaffold Acts as Gatekeeper for Muscle Membrane Growth
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Science Advances study identified an actin scaffold as a gatekeeper for muscle membrane growth. The research addresses how skeletal muscle architecture and membrane development are regulated.

articles.title: Satellite Cell Readiness is Governed by an RNA-Binding Protein in Muscle
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Stem Cell Reports study identified a critical role for the RNA-binding protein TDP-43 in muscle satellite-cell readiness. The findings link TDP-43 with an important aspect of muscle stem-cell biology.

articles.title: Exercise releases protective, muscle-strengthening molecule
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that a molecule released by muscles during exercise enhances muscle function and boosts exercise performance. The finding connects exercise-related muscle signaling with protective and muscle-strengthening effects.

articles.title: Weak Electrical Signals Send Aging Muscle into Decline
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that weak electrical signals are linked to age-related muscle decline. It also notes that age-related muscle wasting may be reversible with targeted pharmaceuticals, based on a new publication and press release.

articles.title: Neanderthal gene linked to more muscle mass in modern humans
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that a Neanderthal gene is linked to higher muscle mass in some modern humans. The result connects inherited ancient genetic material with muscle-related traits today.

articles.title: Brain signaling mechanism may explain clozapine weight gain
articles.summary_3_sentences: UT Southwestern researchers identified a brain signaling pathway that appears to drive clozapine-associated weight gain. The findings are preclinical and point to a possible future strategy for reducing metabolic side effects of clozapine.

articles.title: Disabling a gene brake in pancreatic cells unlocks insulin-producing potential
articles.summary_3_sentences: Harvard Medical School researchers found that tweaking a gene could turn a patient's own pancreatic cells into insulin-producing cells. The work addresses beta-cell shortage, a key feature of both type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

articles.title: Is poor sleep contributing to the country's weight issues?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses whether poor sleep may contribute to weight issues, noting that many teens lose sleep when adapting to fall schedules. It highlights early school start times, demanding classes and adolescent biology as contributors to insufficient sleep.

articles.title: Novo Nordisk Tests Lower-Dose Wegovy Pill for Weight Loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: Novo Nordisk is testing lower maintenance doses of an oral Wegovy formulation in a placebo-controlled study. The trial is evaluating whether lower doses can still support weight loss.

topic_groups.topic: Biomedical AI, Imaging and Research Methods

articles.title: Study identifies key driver of inflammation, opening door to potential new treatments
articles.summary_3_sentences: Johns Hopkins Medicine researchers identified a biological mechanism that helps explain how inflammation is triggered and sustained across a range of diseases. The report describes the mechanism as a possible avenue for future therapeutic development.

articles.title: Formation Bio's Plan to Use AI in Drug Discovery
articles.summary_3_sentences: Formation Bio outlined plans to use artificial intelligence in drug discovery. The company also appointed Dr. Michael Ehlers as chief scientific officer and head of research and development.

articles.title: New Tool for Imaging Cristae Structure & Electrical Flickers
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article presents a new tool for imaging cristae structure and electrical flickers in mitochondria. It addresses visualization of inner mitochondrial membrane ultrastructure and dynamics, a challenge in mitochondrial research.

articles.title: GenAI creates first fully functional synthetic virus genomes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers at Stanford University and the Arc Institute used generative AI to design fully functional synthetic virus genomes. The article presents the work as the first example of this approach producing functional synthetic viral genomes.

articles.title: EasyGrid Simplifies Cryo-Electron Microscopy Sample Preparation
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Nature Methods paper introduced EasyGrid, a method intended to simplify cryo-electron microscopy sample preparation. The method is described as reducing guesswork and time-consuming optimization before imaging.

articles.title: FDA Approves Pasatru for Rare Bone-Forming Disorder
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA approved Regeneron's Pasatru for a rare bone-forming disorder. The drug is intended to reduce new abnormal bone formation and clinician-assessed flare-ups.

articles.title: Human-Guided AI Speeds Up Cell Classification for Spatial Proteomics
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes a human-guided AI approach that speeds cell classification in spatial proteomics. Spatial proteomics allows researchers to combine large numbers of tissue images and protein signals.

articles.title: Endometriosis can elude diagnosis for years. What to know about the disease and new ways to find it
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses how endometriosis can remain undiagnosed for years despite significant symptoms. It also addresses new ways to identify the disease, including the experience of a patient who finally received imaging evidence after years of seeking help.

articles.title: Chemical Exposure Connected to High Blood Pressure in Pregnant Women
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports a connection between exposure to synthetic chemicals in everyday products and high blood pressure in pregnant women. It focuses on pregnancy and cardiovascular health in relation to common chemical exposures.

articles.title: The Gut Microbiome Impacts Uterine Inflammation and Female Reproductive Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Journal of Advanced Research study examined the gut microbiome and uterine inflammation. The study reported that maternal gut dysbiosis increases uterine inflammation, linking gut microbial imbalance with female reproductive health.

topic_groups.topic: Public Health, Policy and Medical Education

articles.title: Smoking's social myth challenged as 50,000-person study links it to loneliness
articles.summary_3_sentences: A large Europe-wide study of 50,000 people linked smoking with increased loneliness. The findings, presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress, challenge the idea that smoking is socially beneficial.

articles.title: End of free school meal program led to increased stress and hunger, poorer diets and reduced focus, say teachers
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers asked teachers what they observed after a pandemic-era universal free school meal program expired in 2022. Teachers reported more student hunger and stress, more junk-food consumption and reduced classroom focus.

articles.title: National call to action needed to strengthen primary care pipeline in medical education, argue experts
articles.summary_3_sentences: A paper led by Hackensack Meridian School of Medicine faculty argues for national action to strengthen the primary care workforce pipeline. The authors outline strategies to improve recruitment beginning in undergraduate medical education.

articles.title: Simple Daily Routine May Improve Sleep, Depression, Heart Health, and More
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that keeping a consistent daily routine may benefit sleep, depression and heart health. It presents regular daily routines as a possible broad health-supporting behavior.
